response.rationale: All three T1 sources are positive (Lyster 2010 found durable corrective-feedback effects, and Adesope 2017 and Hattie 2007 are cited as showing testing and learning effects are strongest with feedback), so the hypothesis is supported. Two of the three entries carry identical text, which suggests duplicated or templated evidence and lowers confidence, and none of the cited text directly measures retention as an outcome of feedback in a predictive sense.
